newsitem.title: FRANCE: France backs Italian government on Albania.
newsitem.headline: France backs Italian government on Albania.

text.p: France voiced confidence on Wednesday that Italy would take part in a security force for Albania as the Rome government put its survival on the line in a gambit to win parliamentary support for the force.
"We are fully confident that Italy will assume its responsibilities," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing.

The first soldiers in France's 1,000-strong contingent for the 6,000-strong Italian-led force that will protect relief convoys in lawless Albania started leaving on Tuesday for the Albanian port of Durres.
The whole French contingent is expected to reach Albania early next week.

Grappling with the worst crisis of his office, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told the lower Chamber of Deputies he would ask President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro to decide his fate if key ally Communist Refoundation carry out their threat to desert him in a vote on the mission later on Wednesday.
Scalfaro, the supreme arbiter in Italian politics, could in such an event either ask Prodi to tender his resignation or send him back to parliament for a confidence vote on the government.
